How do I get tech support or help here?

Many people can and will use this subreddit for questions pertaining to capturing, streaming, or troubleshooting our Game Capture products. We encourage this! We are a community and if someone new is having a little trouble getting started, we should be there to help them out, as every one of us had started out with questions at some point in our capturing careers.

BEFORE YOU ASK FOR HELP, PLEASE check out our knowledge base first at: http://help.elgato.com

Here we have many articles covering many different issues -- Game Capture setup, stream settings, recording party chat on Xbox One/PS4, tips for improving performance, tips for common issues, etc Don’t be surprised if you make a thread and the first response you receive is a link to a knowledge base article. If the tips in the article don’t work, we can go from there. With that being said, the purpose of this thread is to HELP US HELP YOU.

What does this mean exactly? Many times when someone needs help, they can’t express the issue clearly, or they have trouble painting the whole picture. That makes troubleshooting and providing assistance more difficult than it has to be. Having as much information as possible beforehand helps to zero in on the potential issue. If it isn’t mentioned at first, it’s going to be asked before a diagnosis can be given, so this guide will save both you and the helpers’ time.

INFORMATION WE NEED WHEN YOU REQUIRE HELP

  • Your Game Capture Product (Game Capture HD, Game Capture HD60)
  • Your operating system (Windows, Mac, and OS version)
  • Your computer specs (CPU model/clock speed and RAM at a minimum)
  • What you are trying to record? (Console/PC/Mobile)
  • What software you are using? (Game Capture, OBS, XSplit)

Lastly, please mention any other applicable equipment; If you are having issues with live commentary, what type of mic are you using for this? Are you having an issue with video signal and are using an HDMI splitter or switch? Please link us to said equipment. All of this information will help us target the issue you are having. Let’s make this easy and fun for everyone. Help us help you to get everyone streaming and capturing flawlessly.

What are Elgato’s sponsorship requirements?

As much as we would love to sponsor everyone, we have to focus on working with the best personalities or teams that fit our brand and vision. We choose who we sponsor from a variety of factors, including channel size, content type, online persona, target audience and more. We know it’s not fair to judge an individual or a team solely on numbers, so we handle all sponsorship requests on a case by case basis.

If you think you have what it takes and want to become sponsored, you can reach out to the sponsorships team by emailing partnerships@elgato.com

Not sure what to include in your email? If you don’t already have a presentation, here is an easy to follow template:

  • Who are you/your organization?
  • What kind of content do you produce and on what outlets/services?
  • What are the sizes of your audiences on such outlets/services?
  • What platforms do you play on? What types of games do you play?
  • Why you would like a sponsorship/partnership from/with Elgato Gaming?
  • What kind of value or support can you provide Elgato Gaming?
  • What would you like to see in return from Elgato Gaming?
  • What are your relevant social links? (YouTube, Facebook, Twitch, Twitter, Instagram, etc.)

A couple things to think about when submitting:

PLEASE BE BRIEF AND CONCISE. Reading through pages of text will unfortunately make things much more difficult for us to read and review. Short paragraphs and bullet points are your friends. If you don’t have a YouTube or Twitch channel set up yet, it might be best that you build that out for a bit first before reaching out to us. Professionalism, correct spelling and proper grammar all go a long way.

Tell us what your value is to Elgato Gaming. Help us understand what makes your content special. All that will help push your proposal through. Lastly, please understand that we’re a very small team here at Elgato and with the high volume of submissions, we may not be able to reply to every single one. We definitely review every single submission and we ask that you don’t get discouraged if you don’t hear back from us. If we are interested, we’ll absolutely reach out for more information.

The Elgato Gaming Team
